note.note:
History:
- Presenting complaint: Dysuria (burning/stinging on urination), increased urinary frequency, suprapubic/lower abdominal aching, and new pink-tinged urine today.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began just under 1 week ago and have persisted; frequency and dysuria are interfering with university attendance.
- Triggers/timing/associated symptoms: Symptoms worse with voiding. No fever, no chills, no flank/back pain, no nausea or vomiting. No abnormal vaginal discharge reported.
- Sexual/reproductive context: Sexually active with long-term boyfriend; typically no condom use. Last unprotected intercourse approximately 1 week ago. Last menstrual period 2 weeks ago.
- Other relevant history: Tried cannabis once ~1.5 weeks ago (patient-reported; clinician considered unlikely related).

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
- Medications:
  - Combined oral contraceptive pill — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - IBS medication described as starting with "M" — exact name/dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Reported adverse reaction to clindamycin (reaction details not documented).
- Past hospitalizations: Not recorded.

Physical Examination:
- Vital signs: Not recorded.
- Physical exam performed: Not recorded (clinician stated they did not normally examine and was reassured by history).
- Patient-reported/observed findings:
  - No fever reported.
  - No flank or back pain.
  - No nausea or vomiting.
  - No abnormal vaginal discharge.
  - Suprapubic/lower abdominal ache, worse with voiding.
  - Pink-tinged urine noted today.
- Neurologic/mental status: Not recorded (patient conversationally alert and oriented).

Impression:
- Most likely diagnosis: Acute uncomplicated cystitis (bacterial UTI) — history of dysuria, urinary frequency, suprapubic ache, and new hematuria; clinician also assessed this and advised empiric treatment.
- Additional plausible diagnoses consistent with transcript:
  - Urethritis due to sexually transmitted infection (e.g., Chlamydia/Gonorrhea) — medium likelihood given recent unprotected sex and isolated dysuria without clear discharge.
  - Urolithiasis (renal/ureteric stone) — lower likelihood; hematuria can occur but classic flank/colicky pain and vomiting are absent.

Management Plan:
- Immediate/advised treatments:
  - Empiric antibiotic therapy offered: either Trimethoprim OR Nitrofurantoin (Nitrofurantoin described as a three-day course). Dose/route/frequency not documented for either antibiotic.
  - Analgesia advised: Paracetamol for pain — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Hydration: encouraged to drink plenty of fluids.
- Diagnostic testing:
  - Urine sample: patient to provide a urine sample at practice for point-of-care testing and laboratory send-off (urinalysis and culture as available).
- Safety-netting and follow-up:
  - Clinician will contact patient with urine result(s).
  - Return/seek review if symptoms do not improve by one week.
  - Seek urgent review if new fever, flank/back pain, or vomiting develop.
- DDx-informed recommendations supported by transcript:
  - Consider STI testing (NAAT) if symptoms persist, urine culture is negative, or clinically indicated given recent unprotected sex.
  - Consider pregnancy assessment if clinically indicated (clinician noted menstrual history and to bear pregnancy possibility in mind).

Patient Summary:
- 19-year-old female with ~<1 week of dysuria, urinary frequency, suprapubic ache and new pink urine. Clinician suspects uncomplicated cystitis, obtained sexual and menstrual history, advised empiric antibiotics (choice of trimethoprim or nitrofurantoin), urine testing, hydration, and analgesia, with follow-up planned for results or if symptoms worsen.

Key Takeaways:
- Start prescribed antibiotic (Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin) as advised by clinician; exact antibiotic and dose to be confirmed when prescribed.
- Provide a urine sample at the practice today for testing and culture.
- Return urgently for fever, flank/back pain, or vomiting; otherwise follow up if no improvement within one week.

Next Steps:
- Patient to drop off urine sample at designated practice for urinalysis and culture.
- Clinician/practice to review lab results and contact patient with findings and possible antibiotic adjustment based on culture/sensitivity.
- Consider STI NAAT testing if symptoms atypical, persistent, or if urine/culture results suggest; consider pregnancy testing if clinically indicated.
- Follow-up appointment or revisit in 1 week if symptoms unchanged or worse.

Quality checks:
- Missing but expected elements: vital signs, formal physical examination (abdominal, back/flank), documented urinalysis/culture results, pregnancy test result, STI testing status, exact antibiotic choice with dose/route/frequency, paracetamol dose.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted (DDx concurs that acute uncomplicated cystitis is most likely).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear audio and content; occasional repetition and informal phrasing but sufficient for accurate documentation.
